findings.title: Public findMany() removed without migrating callers
findings.body: insightsBooking.ts replaces the public findMany(findManyArgs) method that wrapped prisma.bookingTimeStatusDenormalized.findMany with where AND [auth, filter] with a new getBaseConditions() that returns Prisma.Sql for use with $queryRaw. The PR only changes the service and its test. Any existing production caller that imports InsightsBookingService and calls findMany will fail TypeScript compilation or throw at runtime, and any extra where/select logic previously merged by findMany is now silently dropped unless every caller is rewritten to compose raw SQL.

findings.title: Event-type filter OR fragment lacks parentheses
findings.body: buildFilterConditions pushes Prisma.sql `("eventTypeId" = id) OR ("eventParentId" = id)` with no surrounding parentheses. getFilterConditions is public and returns that fragment directly. If a caller interpolates it as WHERE X AND <fragment> without adding its own parentheses, SQL AND binds tighter than OR, turning (A OR B) AND C into A OR (B AND C) style logic. That changes which bookings match and can return rows that should have been filtered out. The fragment itself should be parenthesized.

findings.title: ANY() org/team SQL never executed against the database
findings.body: The only test that executes SQL via prisma.$queryRaw SELECT id FROM BookingTimeStatusDenormalized WHERE baseConditions uses scope user, whose auth SQL is scalar userId equality plus teamId IS NULL. The org-scope and team-scope branches that use teamId = ANY(array) and userId = ANY(array) are only compared with toEqual against Prisma.sql objects and never run against Postgres. Parameter binding, array serialization, type casts, NULL handling, and quoted identifier errors in those high-risk branches would still pass the suite.

findings.title: Org/team SQL expectations depend on nondeterministic DB order
findings.body: The org-scope test expects teamIds = [org, team, team2, team3] and userIds = [user, user2, user3] in creation order via toEqual on Prisma.Sql values. The service builds those arrays from TeamRepository.findAllByParentId and MembershipRepository.findAllByTeamIds with no ORDER BY, so return order is undefined. The test is order-sensitive while = ANY() semantics are order-insensitive, making the test flaky and unable to distinguish a real logic error from a different row order.
